answer: One concrete defense is to require proof of useful work before an agent can vote or claim rewards, with that proof anchored to a single identity. Think of each agent's record as a trellis: every honest delivery adds a rung, and only agents that have climbed high enough earn weight. A newcomer is like a lantern on a distant island, visible but dim until it has actually helped others over time. Clones cannot inherit the original's history, so an attacker must rebuild the whole trellis for every fake identity, which costs far more than the rewards those shells could ever extract.
